teaser.text: China Petroleum & Chemical Corporation, usually called Sinopec, turns oil and gas into fuel and industrial materials. Its business is easiest to understand as a flow: customers pay for products and services, while crude, energy, labour, transport, maintenance and taxes absorb the money on the way out.

blocks.heading: Where could Sinopec's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is HKD3.51 in October 2027. It falls to HKD3.10 in October 2028 and HKD3.08 in October 2029. The corresponding total returns, including dividends, are negative 16% and negative 18% in the first two years. The 2029 return is negative 13%.
By October 2029, the bear case reaches HKD0.00. The bull case reaches HKD9.07, versus HKD4.53 today. The probabilities are 32% for bear, 50% for base and 18% for bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Sinopec, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base row begins near CNY75,000m and rises only modestly by 2029. The bear row falls from CNY55,000m to CNY44,000m, while the bull row rises from CNY82,000m to CNY100,000m. The base is anchored by the CNY74,420m annualized first-half 2026 result and the CNY75,317m five-year average. The bear reflects weak road-fuel demand, four years of chemical losses and restrained price pass-through. The bull requires better refining margins, utilization and chemical spreads, not merely more capacity. The 2026 programme gives volume targets, but not margin assurance.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Sinopec really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending was RMB133,625 million. Lease payments were RMB19,247 million and interest paid was RMB7,375 million. After those outflows, free cash flow was only RMB2,249 million. Across 2021–2025, the annual figures add to approximately negative RMB81.8 billion.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Sinopec today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price to earnings, divides the share price by annual profit. Sinopec’s trailing P/E was 13.2x, while its forward P/E was 9.4x. The lower forward figure assumes that profits will recover. That can mislead in a cyclical refinery: a business earning HK$10 in a good year and HK$2 in a bad year will look cheapest precisely when its earnings are temporarily strongest.

blocks.heading: How much does Sinopec pay its shareholders per share?

paragraphs.text: The operating margin shrank alongside a five-year revenue decline, while diluted EPS fell each year from 2021 through 2025. The company’s own free cash flow moved from positive in 2021 to negative in 2022–2024, then only RMB2,249 million in 2025 against RMB27,636 million of dividends paid. In 2025, free cash flow per share was RMB0.02 versus RMB0.23 of dividends paid per share.

paragraphs.text: Dividends in the base case hold at CNY0.27 before easing to CNY0.26. The bear declines from CNY0.20 to CNY0.12, while the bull rises from CNY0.30 to CNY0.38. The base begins with the CNY0.40973 next-12-month EPS estimate and the stated 65% payout policy. The downside reflects 2025 free cash flow of only CNY2,249m against dividends paid of CNY27,636m. The upside requires earnings and cash generation to improve together.

The view would move toward the bull case if refining margins remain durable despite softer volumes, chemical utilization improves, and operating cash begins to fund capex and dividends with less borrowing. The key question through October 2029 is therefore whether higher earnings convert into free cash flow rather than being absorbed by investment and distributions.

paragraphs.text: For July through December 2026, Sinopec targeted domestic refined-product sales of 77.68 million tonnes, below the 79.00 million tonnes sold in the first half. Management therefore does not need a second-half rebound to meet its plan.

blocks.heading: What do Sinopec's last eight reported periods show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was RMB729,866 million, above RMB673,696 million a year earlier. Operating income fell from RMB12,528 million to RMB11,479 million. Net income also fell, from RMB9,777 million to RMB8,828 million. Higher sales therefore did not yet produce higher profit.

June-quarter free cash flow reached RMB27,900 million. March-quarter free cash flow was negative RMB39,888 million. Together, the two quarters consumed RMB11,988 million after capital spending, leases and interest.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Sinopec's next results?

paragraphs.text: The central test is whether Sinopec’s expansion is becoming productive growth rather than simply more capacity, more related-party permissions and more dependence on refinancing.
